name: simdutf8 (SIMD UTF-8 validation)
verdict_reason: The README reports up to 23 times faster than std on valid non-ASCII and up to four times on ASCII on Zen2, and up to eleven and four times on Apple M1. The runs date from 2021, but std's validator has not been replaced since: two rewrite PRs (rust-lang/rust #107760 and #136693) were closed unmerged, the second in August 2026.
tier_reason: Benchmark code, data and saved criterion baselines are in the repository, with CPUs, OSes and rustc versions stated.
claimed_speedup: Up to 23 times faster than std on valid non-ASCII and up to four times faster on pure ASCII (x86-64, Zen2); up to eleven times and four times on Apple M1
workload: criterion throughput by charset and input size, from the empty slice to 64 KiB, plus a 64 KiB input whose first character is invalid.
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 3700 (Zen2); Apple M1 MacBook Air
platforms: x86/x86_64 (SSE4.2, AVX2, AVX-512 on Rust 1.89+, runtime detection), aarch64 NEON, wasm32 simd128, armv7 NEON on nightly; no_std; std fallback elsewhere
one_liner: SIMD drop-in for std::str::from_utf8: up to 23x faster on valid non-ASCII text and up to 4x on ASCII for inputs of 64 bytes or more.
how_it_is_fast: It ports simdjson's lookup algorithm: vector table lookups on each byte's nibbles flag invalid sequences 32 or 64 bytes at a time, with an extra pure-ASCII fast path. The basic API only checks an error accumulator at the end, and on x86 the widest supported implementation is picked at runtime.
use_it_when: Validating large buffers of text from network or disk, especially non-ASCII text
Code that calls from_utf8 on every read buffer or record
skip_it_when: Inputs under 64 bytes, which simdutf8 hands to core::str::from_utf8 anyway
Builds with opt-level = "z", which the README says prevents inlining and makes it quite slow
caveats: The 'up to' figures are summaries of charts; per-input numbers are only in chart images and the saved baselines
Measured in 2021; no run on a current rustc was found, although std's validator is essentially unchanged
The compat API, which reports error positions like std, is slightly slower than the basic API
tradeoffs: unsafe SIMD code (the README cites fuzzing and no known bugs)
basic::from_utf8 returns a zero-sized error with no position

evidence.quote: x86-64: Up to 23 times faster than the std library on valid non-ASCII, up to four times faster on ASCII
aarch64: Up to eleven times faster than the std library on valid non-ASCII, up to four times faster on ASCII (Apple Silicon)
X86-64: PC with an AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 3700 CPU (Zen2) on Linux with Rust 1.52.0
Aarch64: Macbook Air with an Apple M1 CPU (Apple Silicon) on macOS with Rust rustc 1.54.0-nightly (881c1ac40 2021-05-08).
For inputs shorter than 64 bytes validation is delegated to `core::str::from_utf8()`
Rewrite UTF-8 validation in shift-based DFA
